domain: food business hygiene inspection ratings / recurrent inspection outcomes
prediction_question: Hypothetical task this source would support (rejected before construction): for a food business establishment in the Food Hygiene Rating Scheme (England/Wales/NI; Scotland runs the parallel FHIS), will its next inspection change its rating band, given its prior rating history, scores and establishment attributes?
prediction_time: The task would need the establishment's prior ratings knowable at a stated instant before the next inspection. The publisher exposes no prior ratings at all (measured), so no such instant can be evidenced from publisher data.
target_definition: Binary: the establishment's next inspection produces a different rating band than its last recorded one. Not derivable from the publisher's data (see rejection_reason).

sources.format: JSON API, versioned via x-api-version header
sources.access: anonymous - API help states 'no sign-up process, API keys, or login details are required'
sources.measured: 363 authorities (Authorities totalCount); establishment schema has exactly one current rating (RatingValue, RatingDate, NewRatingPending, scores) and no history fields

measurements.xml_sample: FHRS760en-GB.xml (Aberdeen City, FHIS): 2,062,982 bytes, ExtractDate 2026-10-21, ItemCount 2,222
measurements.note: API schema and XML extract both carry exactly ONE rating per establishment; no dated historical vintages of the extracts are published anywhere on the publisher's instruments probed

rejection_reason: Target underivable from obtainable data: the publisher exposes exactly one current rating per establishment. The FHRS API v2 establishment schema (measured) carries only the current RatingValue/RatingDate plus NewRatingPending and the three scores - no rating history; the per-authority XML open-data extracts (measured) contain zero history elements and are refreshed current-state snapshots (Header ExtractDate); no dated historical vintages of the extracts are published. Every prospective task on this stream (next-rating change, re-inspection outcome, rating-band duration) needs at least two inspections per establishment from data we can obtain; only self-collection over years could produce that, and self-collected labels can never be verified against the publisher's own record - the same reason the ONS aggregate-grain door is closed. Secondary, not the deciding reason: a next-rating task would also be a task-shape sibling of the published chicago-food-inspections dataset (predict hygiene-inspection outcome from prior inspections), so even with history the novelty case would need arguing against an existing usable form.
next_action: None. Re-open only if the FSA begins publishing per-establishment rating history or dated snapshot vintages of the FHRS/FHIS extracts (check ratings.food.gov.uk/open-data and the API schema for history fields). A self-collected panel is not a re-open path: its labels are unverifiable.
